history.subject: Blueprint: 32 nodes closing the Riemann–Roch chapter's χ-ledger — the cohomological ledger h⁰/h¹/χ with transport along sheaf isomorphisms, the six-term slice of the covariant Ext sequence with its endpoint injectivity/surjectivity and the additivity χ(X₂) = χ(X₁) + χ(X₃), finiteness of divisor-sheaf cohomology by the dévissage induction (with the one-point-divisor calculus and the reusable induction principle), the χ-ledger keystones (χ-step, χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪) + deg D, deg(div g) = 0 with an honest note that the classical source's algebraically-closed statement is not a match, the Riemann inequality, unbounded h⁰), and Riemann–Roch on the challenge curve (the k-linear Γ ≅ k seam, h⁰(𝒪_C) = 1, χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − g, χ(𝒪(D)) = 1 − g + deg D) — the curve-level Riemann inequality anchored to Papaioannou's genus definition (page 7, read). 52 lean anchors, existing nodes reused with no duplicates. Parse ok, 1506 nodes, 0 dangling

Degree lane, first brick: the point divisor as local equations and the divisor class map into the Čech Picard group. pointDivisor — the effective divisor 1·x presented by local equations adapted to a pointed cover: a uniformizer of the DVR stalk spread to a Dedekind chart and isolated to a single zero via finiteness of its principal-divisor support, the constant 1 on the closed complement; regularity stalkwise in the domain, the overlap ratio a unit away from x. divisorClass : CurveDivisor → CechPic as the Finsupp product of pointDivisor classes to ℤ-powers in the commutative group — total on all of CurveDivisor with no effective/anti-effective bookkeeping; additivity divisorClass (D + D') = divisorClass D · divisorClass D' by Finsupp.prod_add_index and zpow arithmetic; the normalization anchor divisorClass (single x 1) = picClass (pointDivisor x). Uniformizer-choice independence deferred by design (available via picClass_rescale when a consumer needs it). The foundation of the E-i..E-iv degree interface, χ-ledger- and (C2)-independent. Picard/PointDivisor.lean; root build 8673 jobs, keystones independently verified axiom-clean

Design: the G-D2 meromorphic-bridge worksheet — the degree lane's gate, de-risked by design. Descoped (T1): the interface consumes only surjectivity (every Čech Picard class of the integral curve is a divisor class) plus the extraction lemma (equal divisor classes differ by a principal divisor); the sheaf-level identification 𝒪(D) ↔ class is consumed nowhere and is parked. The load-bearing structural decision (D1): on an integral scheme every cochain comparison embeds into the function field by germ-at-the-generic-point injectivity — cocycle values, cobounding units, and local equations all live in K(X)ˣ where gluing is literal equality, so no sheaf gluing and no cover-vs-cover comparison anywhere; this is exactly why the bridge is bounded where the (C2) effectivity is a campaign (no descent, one integral curve). Sub-bricks W1–W5: the meromorphic presentation by the base-index trick, the divisor of a presentation (piece-independence by unit ords, finite support by ordZ_support_finite + quasi-compactness), the heart W3 divisorClass(D of presentation) = L via the ord-matching ⇒ unit-ratio local lemma and the rescale/restrict calculus (staged — the balloon risk is isolated here), the extraction lemma in reverse, then classDeg with E-i..E-iii = the recon's G-D3

Design: deg-D4 feasibility recon — the graph divisor is a campaign, not a brick, and the gate stopped the prover as designed. Grep-verified: Mathlib v4.31 has NO effective-Cartier-divisor, NO regular-immersion, and NO scheme-level differentials/conormal API; the only substrate is ring-level (the Kähler diagonal ideal and the standard-smooth cotangent basis — I/I² free of rank 1, one level below what the divisor needs). The deg-D1 gluing template does not transfer: pointDivisor lives on a curve over a FIELD (DVR stalks give the uniformizer); the graph's ambient is the curve over an arbitrary test object, where the generator must come from the relative conormal and its regularity from flatness. Decomposition: deg-D4a LocalEquations.pullback + picClass_pullback (the one bounded χ-independent piece — with the caveat that the naive statement is FALSE without a regularity/flatness hypothesis, pulling a nonzerodivisor along a non-flat map can produce a zerodivisor); deg-D4b the diagonal local equations via standard-smooth charts (Nakayama on the cotangent basis + flatness — worksheet-first campaign); deg-D4c the graph as pullback of the diagonal with base change from the landed section naturality. abelElement is blocked on D4b but NOT on the rank-1 certificate (deferred separately)
